meta.syllabus: Legal Studies: Year 11 per the Legal Studies 11–12 Syllabus (2025, first taught 2027); Year 12 per the Stage 6 Syllabus (2009, last examined 2027)
meta.note: Tag IDs are stable. Question records carry core[] and support[] arrays of these IDs, plus one theme set and one directive. Evidence records carry tags[] of the same IDs. Year 11 tags (inv., dis., chg., exp.) follow the 2025 syllabus; the 2009 Preliminary tags (ls., ind., lip.) were retired on 23 October 2026 and every record was re-tagged.

sectionI.note: Objective response. Questions may refer to stimulus.

sectionIIB.items: one question, no alternative, ~600 words / 4 booklet pages

sectionIII.items: one 25-mark question per option, each with two alternatives; candidates answer two options; ~1000 words / 8 booklet pages each

demandBands.label: Recall & describe
demandBands.expects: Sketches the legal machinery. Accurate content, little judgement.

demandBands.label: Explain & apply
demandBands.expects: Shows how and why the machinery works, with legislation and cases attached to claims.

demandBands.label: Analyse
demandBands.expects: Breaks the issue into parts and shows the relationships between them; competing interests surfaced.

demandBands.label: Evaluate
demandBands.expects: Sustained judgement against criteria, supported throughout by legislation, cases, media and reports.

investigating.label: Investigating the law
investigating.principalFocus: Australia's legal framework and how it has evolved: what law is and does, the criteria used to judge it, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Customary Lore, the sources and institutions of Australian law, the Constitution, the global legal system and legal rights.

outcomes.H1: Identifies and applies legal concepts and terminology
outcomes.H2: Describes and explains key features of and the relationship between Australian and international law
outcomes.H3: Analyses the operation of domestic and international legal systems
outcomes.H4: Evaluates the effectiveness of the legal system in addressing issues
outcomes.H5: Explains the role of law in encouraging cooperation and resolving conflict, as well as initiating and responding to change
outcomes.H6: Assesses the nature of the interrelationship between the legal system and society
outcomes.H7: Evaluates the effectiveness of the law in achieving justice
outcomes.H8: Locates, selects, organises, synthesises and analyses legal information from a variety of sources including legislation, cases, media, international instruments and documents
outcomes.H9: Communicates legal information using well-structured and logical arguments
outcomes.H10: Analyses differing perspectives and interpretations of legal information and issues
outcomes.LST-11-01: describes legal principles and judicial processes used in the legal system
outcomes.LST-11-02: explains the key features of Australian and international law
outcomes.LST-11-03: explains the role, formation and reform of law
outcomes.LST-11-04: analyses differing perspectives of individuals, groups and society in influencing the law
outcomes.LST-11-05: explains methods to resolve conflict and encourage cooperation between individuals, groups and nation-states
outcomes.LST-11-06: analyses legal issues to determine the extent to which the law achieves justice for individuals, groups and society
outcomes.LST-11-07: uses and analyses a range of sources to assess the effectiveness of the law in addressing issues
outcomes.LST-11-08: uses legal concepts to communicate information and legal reasoning to form a judgement
